key_insight: ActCam enables zero-shot joint control of actor motion and per-frame 3D camera parameters, transferring performance from a driving video into a new scene by conditioning a pretrained image-to-video diffusion model on depth and motion cues.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between fine-grained performance control (actor motion) and cinematographic control (camera intrinsics/extrinsics) in video generation without requiring dataset-specific fine-tuning.
method: Extract 3D motion and scene depth cues from a driving video to represent the actor's performance and geometry.
Inject per-frame intrinsic and extrinsic camera parameters as conditioning signals into a pretrained image-to-video diffusion backbone.
Perform zero-shot joint transfer to synthesize a novel scene that preserves the driving motion and follows the specified camera trajectory.
impact: Provides a practical, training-free way to generate cinematic, controllable videos—useful for filmmakers, animators, and researchers creating synthetic datasets or studying controllable video synthesis.

paper_title: ActCam: Zero-Shot Joint Camera and 3D Motion Control for Video Generation
paper_authors: Omar El Khalifi, Thomas Rossi, Oscar Fossey, Thibault Fouque, Ulysse Mizrahi
